neighborhoods.name: Short Hills & Deerfield
neighborhoods.character: World-renowned luxury enclave with sprawling estate properties, historic colonials, English Tudors, and country estates
neighborhoods.description: One of America's wealthiest residential communities, founded as a planned arboretum suburb with private country clubs and top-ranked public schools.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Highest average property tax bills in New Jersey, routinely exceeding ,000 to ,000+ per estate.

neighborhoods.name: Wyoming Historic District
neighborhoods.character: Historic neighborhood nestled against South Mountain Reservation, featuring turn-of-the-century Victorians and classic colonials
neighborhoods.description: Historic enclave bordering the reservation, prized for historic gaslamps, architectural preservation, and jitney service to Millburn station.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Stable ratables with low appeal volatility and fierce community support for school funding.

neighborhoods.name: Millburn Center & Downtown
neighborhoods.character: Walkable village center with boutique shops, fine dining, Paper Mill Playhouse, and walk-to-train residences
neighborhoods.description: Cultural heart anchored by the State Theatre of New Jersey (Paper Mill Playhouse) and midtown direct train commuting.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Strong retail core bolstered by The Mall at Short Hills (one of the nation's premier luxury retail centers).

equityAnalysis.summary: Millburn Township (Short Hills) maintains a certified residential tax roll across its neighborhoods.

keyTakeaways.title: Property Tax Burden & Household Income
keyTakeaways.detail: In Millburn Township (Short Hills), homeowners pay an average of $23,675.96 annually in property taxes, consuming approximately 9.47% of median household income.

keyTakeaways.title: Equalization Ratio & Revaluation Balance
keyTakeaways.detail: With an equalization ratio of 88.5%, assessed values average ~88.5% of current true market values, establishing the basis for certified county tax equalization.

keyTakeaways.title: School District vs Municipal Levy Split
keyTakeaways.detail: Local education represents 63.8% of the total tax bill, municipal government absorbs 20.4%, and Essex County claims 15.8%.
